grades.quote: If access to the cache block is not permitted, a cache-block management instruction raises a store page-fault or store guest-page-fault exception if address translation does not permit any access or raises a store access-fault exception otherwise.
grades.reason: This RISC-V passage covers only CBO (cache-block) instructions. It separates a page-fault, which comes from address translation, from an access-fault, which comes from PMP/PMA. It also says the faulting address is written to *tval. It does not explain how to tell a missing mapping (invalid PTE) from insufficient page permissions, since both are page faults. It is limited, tangential help.
This is a back-of-book index fragment with terms such as page fault and page table. It has no explanation of how to tell a permission fault from a missing mapping.
